name: guilt
description: Dismay or sadness from a perception that your behavior did not meet one of your own important principles.
perceptions: One of my actions or inaction did not match with an important rule I strive to live by.

guidance.description: Guilt is an emotion that involves feelings of remorse and self-judgment. While it can be a helpful emotion for personal growth, letting it linger too long can take a toll on your emotional health.

examples: I should have invited John too.

comparisons.description: Guilt is a self-recognition of behavior that did not meet an internal expectation, while shame is a perception of losing status from not meeting an important external rule. Guilt and shame could certainly come together if your internal expectation matches the external rule.
Embarrassment is a relatively minor discomfort about failing to meet social expectations. Guilt is a more significant experience from failing to meet one your own important standards.

commentaries.quote: I'm just going to say it: I'm pro-guilt. Guilt is good. Guilt helps us stay on track because it's about our behavior. It occurs when we compare something we've done—or failed to do—with our values.
Guilt upon the conscience, like rust upon iron, both defiles and consumes it, gnawing and creeping into it, as that does which at last eats out the very heart and substance of the metal.
Habitual guilt points to where you expect yourself to be pure and perfect. Perhaps it's an unconscious way of doing penance in hopes of being forgiven by existence.
